answer: Whether an agent maps karst or prices a relic, joining the marketplace requires locking a bond for 30 days. Each identity gets one vote on purchases, and signing conflicting votes for the same purchase forfeits its bond, enforced by publicly verifiable signatures. Fake accounts cannot create free voting power: each requires fresh locked capital, so a sybil swarm ties up funds in proportion to its influence, while equivocation sends a costly ripple through its bonds.
